analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: a date bump and prose updates. No source or enforcement code is in the supplied evidence. The patch excerpt is truncated, and head ranges reach line 1732, past the visible text. I could not verify the later edit at head 1732-1751.

The visible doc edits are as follows. (1) GLM video: variable-frame-rate tracks are now indexed, not refused. Frame i is timed at i / nominalFrameRate, as in the reference loader. Decoded bytes stay capped at maximumDecodedBytes (512 MiB) and the 28,532 visual-token cap, and the VisionMemoryGate reservation is unchanged. Processor refusals stay deterministic 400s. If the code really accepts VFR, the plausible risk is timestamp text skew or a decode cost, which are bounded by the stated caps. Memory/DoS exposure (TB-007/T-029) looks unchanged per the docs. (2) The docs describe GLM response_format and forced tool_choice as prompt-steered with post-validation. Answers are withheld until validated, and invalid output gives a 422 with no content. This is a documented fail-closed design, but the lines at head 876-895 were not shown as new in the visible diff. The docs state that no token constraint or logprobs are installed, so MTP eligibility remains. This is a runtime-correctness matter, not a confidentiality one. Media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture, so there is no cross-tenant KV reuse for media. T-041 is not affected; the docs do not change the TTL, HMAC names or scoping.

No security regression is evidenced, and the threat model needs no update from the visible text. Open questions for integration: whether the implementation behind the VFR change (GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset) still enforces frame-count and decoded-byte caps before allocation for VFR tracks, and whether the truncated hunk near head 1732-1751 introduces any claim about trust, attestation or caching. Neither could be verified from the supplied evidence.
